The -a ending is the standard past tense 3rd person masculine singular marker. The verb conveys the sense of something descending into actuality — an event landing, a word or decree being realised.
1.root: و-ق-ع (w-q-') — to fall, to occur, to come to pass

2.meaning: The word, the saying, the utterance — a statement or pronouncement; qawl is speech that has been spoken, and 'the word' can mean a settled decree or verdict.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; a saying, statement, or pronouncement.

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
4.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

5.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
5.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

6.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
6.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: They speak, articulate, utter intelligible words; the capacity for meaningful speech. A present-tense verb of speaking in the third-person masculine plural.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural: the 'ya-' prefix plus the '-ūna' ending together mean 'they (men) …', and the retained final '-na' marks the ordinary (indicative) present of an ongoing or habitual action.
8.root: ن-ط-ق (n-ṭ-q) — to speak, articulate, give voice to intelligible words

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, behold

3.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
3.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

4.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

5.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
5.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').
5.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, darkness

6.meaning: So that they may rest, dwell, or find tranquillity — the verb sakana encompasses the ideas of settling, residing, being still, and finding peace or calm.

parts.en: so that, in order that (lām of purpose)
they rest, dwell, find calm (subjunctive stem)
subjunctive plural ending (3rd person masculine plural, nūn dropped)

6.grammar: The lām of purpose (li-) governs the imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood. The prefix ya- marks 3rd person masculine plural with the -ū suffix (the subjunctive plural ending where the final nūn is dropped). In the subjunctive, the indicative ending -u of the singular stem is replaced by the subjunctive -a before the plural suffix, yielding yaskunū. The lām + subjunctive construction expresses purpose: 'in order that they may rest/dwell'. The verb's core sense spans physical rest, psychological tranquillity, and dwelling in a place.
6.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to dwell, to find calm

7.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

8.meaning: And the daytime — the period of daylight between dawn and sunset, the bright span of the day as opposed to night.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the definite article (here assimilated as n-nahār). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb or the thing being pointed to.

9.meaning: Giving light to see by — making things visible, illuminating so that sight is possible. The active participle describes something that grants visibility or causes one to see clearly.
9.grammar: An active participle of form IV (the mu- prefix marks 'the one doing/causing the action'). The -an ending marks the accusative with indefiniteness, commonly used for a descriptive state ('as something giving light'), and the final -n (nunation) signals 'a/some'.
9.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, to perceive, sight

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
13.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.
13.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

14.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
14.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

15.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
15.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

2.meaning: It is blown / breathed into — a passive verb meaning that air or breath is forced into something, especially the blowing of a horn or trumpet to produce a sound.
2.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'it is blown.' The yu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern marks the passive (the action is done to the subject, not by it). The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a simple statement of fact rather than a command or negation.
2.root: ن-ف-خ (n-f-kh) — to blow, breathe, or puff air into

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The horn or trumpet — the great horn that is sounded; also the natural sense of a horn-shaped instrument blown to summon or signal.
4.grammar: Definite noun ('the trumpet'). The al- prefix means 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
4.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — form, shape; here a horn or trumpet

5.meaning: And he/it was terrified, startled, or thrown into alarm — the verb fazi'a denotes the sudden onset of fear or fright, the jolt of terror.

parts.en: he was terrified, he was alarmed (past tense verb)

5.grammar: The conjunction fa- ('and so'/'then', marking a consequence or sequence) prefixed to the Form I verb fazi'a in the perfect (past) tense, 3rd person masculine singular. The -a ending marks the past tense 3rd person masculine singular. The verb describes the experience of being seized by sudden, alarming fear.
5.root: ف-ز-ع (f-z-') — to be frightened, to be startled, to be alarmed

6.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
6.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
8.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
9.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
11.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
13.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
13.root: — (pronoun)

14.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
14.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: 'And all / and each / every one' — kull denotes totality or completeness: the whole of a group ('all') or every single member taken individually ('each one').
16.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The noun is indefinite and in the nominative case, the form used for a subject. The closing -un is nunation ('-un'); standing alone with nunation it carries the sense 'each one / all of them'.
16.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — all, whole, the totality, each

17.meaning: They came to him, they arrived before him — the act of approaching and presenting oneself before someone, especially in submission or obedience.

parts.en: they came, they arrived (3rd person masculine plural past)
him (3rd person masculine singular direct object pronoun)

17.grammar: The Form I verb atā ('to come') in the perfect (past) tense, 3rd person masculine plural. The base form atā contracts when the plural suffix -ū is added, giving ataw-. The final -ū becomes -aw before the object pronoun -hu. The suffix -hu is the direct object pronoun 'him'. Together: 'they came to him'.
17.root: أ-ت-و (ā-t-w) — to come, to arrive, to bring

18.meaning: Humbled, subdued, in a state of abasement — referring to those who are brought low and rendered abjectly subservient, stripped of pride or resistance.
18.grammar: An active participle (Form I, fāʿil pattern) meaning 'one who is humbled/abased', used here in the masculine plural. The ending -īna is the masculine sound plural genitive/accusative ending, used when the word functions as an object, complement, or falls under a governing element. It describes a group of beings in a state of complete submission and abasement.
18.root: د-خ-ر (d-kh-r) — to be abased, to be humbled, to be subservient

1.meaning: "and you see / would see" — to perceive with the eyes or to behold; also "to regard" something as being a certain way.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second-person masculine singular: the ta- prefix means "you (one man)." This verb comes from a weak root, so its final weak letter shows as the long -ā vowel; in the indicative it expresses ongoing or potential seeing.

2.meaning: The mountains — large natural elevations of rock and earth. A plural noun made definite by 'the'.
2.grammar: A definite plural noun. The prefixed al- means 'the'. The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
2.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain; by extension that which is firmly fixed or innate

3.meaning: You suppose them, you consider them, you think them (to be something) — the verb ḥasiba means to reckon, calculate, or assume something to be a certain way.

parts.en: you suppose, you consider (2nd person singular imperfect)
them/it (3rd person feminine singular or plural direct object pronoun)

3.grammar: The Form I verb ḥasiba ('to reckon, to suppose, to consider') in the present/imperfect tense, 2nd person masculine singular. The prefix ta- marks the subject as 'you' (singular). The -u ending is the indicative imperfect vowel, signalling an ongoing or present action. The suffix -hā is the 3rd person feminine singular/plural object pronoun, 'it/them'. Together: 'you consider them (to be)'.
3.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, to suppose, to calculate

4.meaning: Stationary, fixed, motionless — describing something that is solid, still, or frozen in place, giving the appearance of being immovable.
4.grammar: A feminine active participle (Form I, fāʿila pattern) in the indefinite accusative case, marked by the tanwīn fatḥ (-an). The accusative here marks a predicate complement or hal (circumstantial description). The word describes something in a state of stillness or apparent solidity, as opposed to being in motion.
4.root: ج-م-د (j-m-d) — to solidify, to be still, to freeze

5.meaning: and it / and she — the conjunction 'and' joined to a standalone subject pronoun meaning 'it' or 'she', pointing to something feminine in gender.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The word hiya is an independent subject pronoun for a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) entity, 'it/she'. As a standalone pronoun it typically begins a descriptive statement about that thing.
5.root: — (conjunction with pronoun)

6.meaning: It passes, it moves along, it goes by — the verb marra conveys steady movement or passage, something drifting or gliding past.

parts.en: it passes, it moves along (3rd person feminine singular imperfect)

6.grammar: The Form I verb marra ('to pass, to go by') in the present/imperfect tense, 3rd person feminine singular. The prefix ta- marks the subject as feminine singular ('it', referring to a feminine noun). The -u ending is the indicative imperfect vowel, marking an ongoing or habitual action. The doubling of the final rā' (marra) is intrinsic to this root's geminate (doubled-letter) pattern.
6.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass, to go by, to move along

7.meaning: he passed / he passed by — a third-person past verb meaning to go past, to pass through or by a place or thing.
7.grammar: A past tense verb with a third-person singular masculine doer ('he'). The doubled final consonant reflects the root's repeated letter. The final -a marks the third-person singular masculine subject. It states a completed action: 'he passed'.
7.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass, to pass by

8.meaning: The clouds — masses of condensed water vapour gathered in the sky, capable of bringing rain. The root sense is 'that which is drawn or trailed across', reflecting the clouds' drifting motion.
8.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- (the lām assimilates to the shamsī letter sīn, giving al-saḥāb). The -i ending is the genitive case vowel, indicating that this word is governed by what precedes it — typically a preposition or a noun in an iḍāfa (construct) relationship. Saḥāb is a collective noun; its singular would be saḥāba.
8.root: س-ح-ب (s-ḥ-b) — to draw, to drag; clouds are 'that which is drawn across the sky'

9.meaning: The work, the craftsmanship, the making — the product of careful and deliberate manufacture; the result of skilled, purposeful creation.
9.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) in the accusative case, here without tanwīn because it is in an iḍāfa (construct) — its definiteness comes from the noun that follows it (the one whose work it is). The -a ending is the accusative case vowel. Used in the accusative as a cognate object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) or a noun of specification, highlighting the quality and nature of the act of making.
9.root: ص-ن-ع (ṣ-n-') — to make, to craft, to manufacture skillfully

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A relative pronoun, masculine singular, meaning 'who / which / the one that.' It links a following clause to a noun, marking it out as 'the [noun] that…'
11.grammar: A masculine-singular relative pronoun. It is indeclinable (its form does not change for case) and introduces a description, equivalent to 'the one who/which…'

12.meaning: He perfected, He made firm and exact — the verb atqana means to execute something with the highest precision, leaving no flaw or looseness; to bring something to a state of complete soundness.

parts.en: he perfected, he made precise and firm (Form IV past tense)

12.grammar: A Form IV verb (atqana — to perfect, to make firm) in the perfect (past) tense, 3rd person masculine singular. The -a ending marks the past tense 3rd person masculine singular. Form IV (af'ala) typically imparts a causative or intensive sense: not merely 'to be firm' but 'to bring something to firmness and precision'. This word implies mastery and meticulous care in execution.
12.root: ت-ق-ن (t-q-n) — firmness, precision, perfection in craft

13.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
13.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.
13.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — wholeness, totality

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
15.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

16.meaning: 'Fully aware / All-Aware' — one who knows the inner reality and hidden details of things through intimate, expert knowledge. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect awareness of all that is concealed.
16.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, thorough quality ('thoroughly aware'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamm): it marks an indefinite noun/adjective in the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

17.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
17.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

18.meaning: To do, perform, or carry out an action; to act. The most general verb for engaging in any deed, good or bad.
18.grammar: A present/imperfect verb meaning 'you (plural) do'. The ta-…-ūna frame marks the subject as 'you all'; the full ending -ūna (with its final nūn intact) is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action.

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

3.meaning: 'With / for the good deed' — the noun ḥasana (a good deed, a fine thing, a benefit) made definite ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('with/for/by'). It denotes a beautiful or beneficial act or reward.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with/for') and the article al- ('the'). The final -i marks the genitive case, which is required after a preposition. The feminine -a(t) ending is built into the word.

4.meaning: So for him / then his is; a linking word 'so/then' joined to 'for him,' expressing that something belongs or accrues to a single male — 'so to him belongs…'
4.grammar: A cluster of particles: the connector fa- ('so, then, and as a result') + the preposition la- ('for, belonging to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). Together they assign possession or entitlement to a single male: 'so for him (is)…'

5.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
5.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
5.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

6.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
6.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.

7.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
7.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: Terror, fright, alarm — the intense inner shock and fear that seizes a person, especially in the face of something overwhelming or catastrophic.
9.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar/noun) in the indefinite genitive case, marked by the tanwīn kasr (-in). The genitive indicates that this word is governed by a preposition or is part of an iḍāfa. The tanwīn marks it as indefinite. The word denotes the emotion and experience of sudden, overwhelming fear.
9.root: ف-ز-ع (f-z-') — to be frightened, to be alarmed, to be in terror

10.meaning: On that Day — a compound temporal expression pointing to a specific, momentous Day, combining 'day' with a reference to a previously mentioned time.

parts.en: day (accusative, acting as a time adverb)
then, at that time (temporal particle, indefinite genitive)

10.grammar: A compound temporal adverb: yawma ('day', in the accusative used as a time adverb — ẓarf zamān) combined with idhin ('at that time', a particle that takes the tanwīn kasr -in when not followed by a full clause). Together yawma-idhin means 'on that Day' — referring back to a specific time already in the discourse. The -a on yawma is the plain accusative case vowel (not tanwīn; yawma is in construct with idhin and therefore carries no tanwīn); the -in on idhin is the genitive tanwīn of the standalone particle.

11.meaning: Safe, secure, free from fear — those who are in a state of security and peace, having been granted safety from harm or terror.

parts.en: safe, secure (masculine plural nominative active participle stem)

11.grammar: An active participle (Form I, fāʿil pattern) meaning 'one who is safe/secure', in the masculine sound plural nominative form. The ending -ūna is the masculine plural nominative, used when the word functions as the subject or predicate of a sentence. It describes a group of people who are in an ongoing state of safety and freedom from fear.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

3.meaning: 'With / for the evil deed' — the noun sayyi'a (a bad deed, an evil or harmful thing) made definite ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('with/for/by'). It is the counterpart of the 'good deed.'
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with/for') and the article (written al- but pronounced as-sayyi'a because the s is a 'sun letter' that absorbs the l). The final -i marks the genitive case, required after a preposition. The feminine -a(t) ending is built in.

4.meaning: And they will be cast down, flung headlong — the verb kubba in its passive form means to be hurled or thrown down onto one's face, a vivid image of violent humiliation and downfall.

parts.en: they (feminine/it) were cast down headlong (passive past tense)

4.grammar: The conjunction fa- ('and so'/'then') prefixed to the Form I verb kabb in the passive perfect tense, 3rd person feminine (singular or plural collective). The passive is indicated by the ḍamma on the first letter (ku-) and fatḥa on the doubled consonant (-bba-). The -t ending marks the feminine gender of the subject. The verb vividly describes being thrown violently face-forward or headlong, a gesture of utter disgrace.
4.root: ك-ب-ب (k-b-b) — to throw headlong, to overturn, to cast face-down

5.meaning: Their faces — the plural 'faces' joined to a possessive 'their', i.e. the faces belonging to a group of people.
5.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u before the suffix is the nominative ending, marking the word as a subject or topic. The suffix -hum means 'their' (referring to a group of males or a mixed group): 'their faces'.
5.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, aspect

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
7.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

8.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
8.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

9.meaning: 'You are recompensed / repaid' — a passive verb meaning a group is given back what their deeds deserve, whether reward or penalty. The doer (the One who repays) is understood, not named.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb (form I). The tu- prefix with passive vowelling plus the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject being acted upon ('you [all] are repaid'). The -una (not -u) shows the indicative mood, used for plain factual statements.
9.root: ج-ز-ى (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
12.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

13.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: 'I was commanded', 'I have been ordered / instructed'. It expresses that the speaker is the recipient of a command — someone else has issued an order and the speaker is bound by it.

parts.en: passive vowel: the action was done to the subject

2.grammar: Past-tense passive verb. The -tu ending means the subject is 'I', and the opening u-vowel makes it passive ('I was commanded' rather than 'I commanded'). The action is presented as completed.
2.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order, instruct

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'That I worship / serve' — to worship, to serve in humble devotion and obedience as a servant before his Master.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, taken when the verb is governed by a preceding particle (such as 'that/to'), giving the sense 'that I worship' or 'to worship'.

5.meaning: Lord, Master, Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings a thing to its completion; far richer than 'lord', it joins ownership, care, and continual upbringing of all that He sustains.
5.grammar: A noun ending in -a, marking the accusative case — the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb (e.g. of 'I fear') or when it is being addressed/specified into that case. It carries no prefix or article in this form.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

6.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
6.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

7.meaning: the city; the town — a settled, inhabited place; often carries the sense of a central, established urban community
7.grammar: Definite feminine noun in the genitive case. The -i ending (kasrah) is the genitive marker, which typically signals that the noun follows a preposition or is in a possessive (idāfa) construction — linking it to what governs it as 'of the city' or 'of/in/to the city'.

8.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

9.meaning: He made it sacred / He declared it inviolable — the act of rendering something forbidden, protected, and set apart as a sanctified zone where ordinary permissions do not apply

parts.en: it / her (3rd person feminine singular object pronoun)

9.grammar: Form II (faʿʿala) perfect (past) tense, 3rd person masculine singular verb. The doubled middle radical (r-r) gives Form II its intensifying or causative force — not merely 'forbid' but 'cause to be inviolable / declare definitively sacred'. The suffix -hā is the direct object pronoun referring back to a feminine noun (such as 'the city/land'), meaning 'it' or 'her'.

10.meaning: And for him / and he has — the connector 'and', the preposition 'for/to', and the pronoun 'him'. Together it expresses possession or belonging ('and to him belongs …', 'and he has …').
10.grammar: A small phrase, not a verb: the connector wa- ('and') + the preposition la- ('for/to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). The preposition with a pronoun commonly conveys having or belonging ('he has', 'belonging to him').

11.meaning: A quantifying noun meaning 'each', 'every', or 'all'. When joined to a following noun it sweeps that noun up in its entirety or distributes over every instance of it ('every man', 'all of it'); it expresses totality or comprehensiveness.
11.grammar: A noun used to quantify. The final -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as standing independently. It is normally placed before a noun in the genitive ('all OF …', 'every …').

12.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
12.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

13.meaning: And I have been commanded — a past-tense statement in which the speaker reports being ordered or instructed by another; the doer of the commanding is left unnamed, so the focus rests on the speaker as the one under orders.
13.grammar: A past-tense passive verb with the prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The inner vowel pattern 'u-i' shows it is passive ('was commanded', no named commander), and the '-tu' ending makes the speaker its subject ('I was commanded').
13.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; an affair or matter

14.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
14.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
14.root: — (particle; no root)

15.meaning: '(that) I be / I should be' — the verb 'to be/become' in the first person, used in a dependent sense ('that I be…', 'lest I be…'). It expresses entering into or belonging to a described state.

parts.en: be / become (stem, ending in the subjunctive vowel -a)

15.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be/become' with the 'I' prefix (a-). The stem ends in the third root letter ن, which carries the final short vowel -a; this -a is the subjunctive ending, the form used after particles such as 'that', 'so that', or 'lest' — so it reads 'that I be / I should be' rather than the plain statement 'I am' (which would end in -u).
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

16.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
16.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

17.meaning: The ones who submit/surrender — those who give themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience and peace (the Muslims). As an active participle it names people characterized by this submission.
17.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem is the Form IV active participle 'one who submits/surrenders'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (the form used after prepositions, as object, or when linked to a preceding noun); its nominative counterpart would be -ūna. So: 'the ones who submit'.

1.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
1.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

2.meaning: I recite / I follow and read aloud — the act of reciting a text carefully, following its sequence faithfully; in Qur'anic usage it conveys both the faithful reading of revelation and following it closely

parts.en: recite / follow in sequence (stem, with subjunctive fatha on the wāw)
alif fariqah (silent orthographic alif; not pronounced, not the mood marker)

2.grammar: Form I imperfect (present/future) verb, 1st person singular, in the subjunctive mood (manṣūb). The initial a- prefix marks the subject as 'I'. The subjunctive is marked by the short fatha (-a) on the wāw of the stem — not by the following alif. That final alif is the alif fariqah, a scribal convention used in Qur'anic and classical orthography after wāw-final verb forms to distinguish them visually; it is entirely silent and carries no morphological value. The subjunctive mood appears after certain particles (such as ʾan, li, etc.) that pull the verb into a subordinate construction conveying purpose or indirect command ('that I recite / to recite').
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to follow, to recite, to read in sequence

3.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Scripture; literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading'.
3.grammar: A definite noun (carrying 'al-', 'the') on the verbal-noun pattern fuʿlān, denoting the act/thing of reciting. The final '-a' marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the word is the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — reciting, reading aloud, gathering words together

4.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then whoever'. It joins a clause to what precedes ('so', 'then') and introduces a conditional or general statement about any person who does something ('whoever, anyone who').
4.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so/then', linking this to a prior statement. man is a conditional/relative word for persons ('whoever'); its base form is man, and the final vowel here is read -i simply to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster, not a case ending.

5.meaning: He became guided / found the right way / accepted guidance — the verb (Form VIII) means to take the right path, follow guidance, and be rightly directed; it implies responding to and embracing guidance.

parts.en: became guided / followed the right way

5.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the Form VIII pattern (which often carries a reflexive sense — accepting guidance for oneself), with a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). Its weak final root letter appears as a long -ā ending, the usual past-tense shape for such roots.
5.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

6.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
6.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

7.meaning: He is guided / follows the right way — the present-tense counterpart of the same Form VIII verb: to take guidance, be rightly directed, and follow the correct path.

parts.en: be guided / follow the right way (Form VIII stem)

7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the Form VIII pattern (often reflexive — taking guidance for oneself). The ya- prefix marks a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). The root's weak final letter surfaces as a long -ī, and this full ending reflects the ordinary indicative (a plain statement).
7.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

8.meaning: For / to himself / for his own soul — nafs means the self, soul, or person (the inner self that is held to account). The li- means 'for/to,' and the attached -hi makes it 'his.'
8.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('for/to') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). After the preposition the noun is in the genitive, shown by the -i vowel before the -hi suffix.
8.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person, the inner being

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
9.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

10.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

11.meaning: Then say! / so say!: a command to one person to speak or utter, joined to what precedes by 'then/so'.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male, 'say!' The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then' or 'so', linking the command to something before it as a consequence or sequel. The bare, vowel-less ending is normal for this imperative.

12.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
12.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

13.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
13.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: The warners / those who give warning — the definite plural active participle of 'to warn'; describes prophets and messengers who deliver warnings from Allah.

parts.en: the warners (Form IV active participle, masculine plural genitive/accusative)

15.grammar: The -īna ending is masculine sound plural genitive/accusative. al-mundhirīna is the definite Form IV active participle (muf'il pattern) of n-dh-r: those who give solemn warning.
15.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, to vow; a warner

1.meaning: "And say" — a command addressed to one male to speak or proclaim words.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a single male ("you"). The base imperative is qul; the final -i here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster — it is not a case or tense ending.

2.meaning: All praise, commendation, and grateful acknowledgement — the recognition that beauty, goodness, and perfection rightly belong to and are owed to the one being praised. As a definite noun with the article 'al-', it conveys that the totality of praise is encompassed.
2.grammar: A definite noun (carrying the article 'al-', 'the'). The final '-u' ending is nominative: it marks the word as the subject or main topic of a statement — the thing being talked about or the doer of an action, rather than its object.
2.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise, to commend, to give thanks

3.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

4.meaning: He will show you (all) — a promise or statement that something will be displayed or made evident to a group; the showing involves causing something to become visible or clearly perceived

parts.en: he shows / causes to see (stem, Form IV)
you (all) — 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun

4.grammar: Form IV (afʿala) imperfect (present-future) verb, 3rd person masculine singular, with the near-future prefix sa- and an attached direct object pronoun -kum (you all / you plural). The sa- prefix narrows the imperfect's broad present-future meaning to a definite near future: 'He will indeed show'. The -kum suffix identifies the recipients of the showing as a masculine plural group ('you').
4.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, to perceive, to show

5.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
5.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

6.meaning: and you will recognise them / and you will come to know them — the act of recognising or identifying something by its distinguishing features, recalling or confirming what one already knows

parts.en: you (all) will recognise / know (stem, Form I imperfect)
it / her (3rd person feminine singular object pronoun)

6.grammar: Form I imperfect (present-future) verb, 2nd person masculine plural, indicative mood, with an attached direct object pronoun. The ta- prefix and -ūna ending together mark the subject as 'you (plural)'. The fa- prefix is a consequential particle ('and so', 'thereupon'), indicating that the recognition follows as a result of the showing. The suffix -hā is strictly the 3rd person feminine singular object pronoun; any collective or plural sense in the translation ('them') derives from the grammatical gender of the referent noun, not from the pronoun itself, which is morphologically singular feminine.
6.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, to recognise, to be acquainted with

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

8.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
8.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

9.meaning: 'With/being heedless' — the preposition/particle 'bi' attached to 'ghāfil', one who is unaware, inattentive, or neglectful, failing to take notice.
9.grammar: The particle 'bi-' governs the following word into the genitive case. 'Ghāfil' is an active participle ('one who is heedless'). The '-in' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive; the 'bi-' here commonly adds emphasis within a negation ('not at all heedless').

10.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
10.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

11.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds
